First Aid Provision: Who to Contact

Purpose and scope

This guidance sets out first aid provision at every Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift, ensuring appropriate first aid cover is always available.

Policy statement

Every shift has access to a trained first aider and a stocked first aid box, so that an injury to a resident, staff member or visitor can be responded to promptly and competently.

Definitions

**First aider** a staff member holding a current first aid at work qualification. **Appointed person** a staff member responsible for calling emergency services and looking after first aid equipment, where a full first aider is not required by the site's risk assessment. **First aid box** the stocked, clearly labelled box maintained at each site.

1. Ensure at least one qualified first aider is on duty for every shift, based on the site's own risk assessment of resident numbers and needs.
2. Check the first aid box monthly, restocking any used or expired item promptly.
3. Record every first aid incident, however minor, in the accident book kept alongside the first aid box.
4. Call emergency services immediately for any injury beyond what first aid can safely manage.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (governing the wider incident record a first aid event also feeds into) and the Health and Safety Policy (the broader risk assessment first aid provision sits within).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates prompt response. A staff member cuts their hand while assisting in the kitchen. The on-duty first aider treats the cut using the first aid box, records it in the accident book, and confirms the box needs a replacement dressing at the next monthly check.

Frequently asked questions

**Does every single staff member need a first aid qualification?** No, only enough trained first aiders to meet the site's risk assessment for every shift; other staff know who the first aider on duty is. **What happens if the qualified first aider is off sick unexpectedly?** The registered manager arranges cover from another qualified first aider, including from a neighbouring site if needed for that shift.

Training and competency

First aiders renew their qualification before it expires, tracked centrally by HR alongside the wider Mandatory Training Matrix.

Locating first aid equipment across a larger site

A larger site such as Harbour View holds a first aid box at more than one location given its size, and staff are shown the location nearest their usual working area during induction so a first aider is never searching for equipment while also managing an active injury.

Closing note

Prompt, competent first aid response depends on the right person and the right equipment being available every shift, and this guidance exists to make sure that is never left to chance.

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how staff complete a body map when they notice or are told about a mark, bruise or skin change on a resident. It applies to every care staff member.

Policy statement

A body map provides a clear, dated, consistent record of a mark's location, size and appearance, supporting both good skin care and, where relevant, a safeguarding referral, since a vague written description alone can be hard to compare accurately over time.

Definitions

Purpose and scope

This manual consolidates Alderbridge Care Group's full health and safety framework into a single

Policy statement

Alderbridge is committed to providing a safe working and living environment for staff, residents and
visitors, now with an annual health and safety report appendix standardising exactly what is presented to
the Board each year across every area this manual covers.

Definitions

**Risk assessment** the structured process of identifying a hazard and the control measure needed to
manage it. **Cyber and data risk** the area recognising that a system outage or data loss can directly
affect resident safety. **Annual health and safety report** the new standardised appendix, introduced in
this version, consolidating a year's data across every area into one comparable format.

Roles and responsibilities

**The Chief Executive** holds ultimate accountability for health and safety. **Each registered manager**
holds day-to-day responsibility for their site's compliance and contributes site-level data to the new annual
report. **Facilities, IT and the Quality Lead** jointly compile the new annual report using the standardised
template.

1. Complete and regularly review a risk assessment for every significant work activity and area.

2. Report a workplace incident or near miss through the Incident Reporting Policy.

3. Provide health and safety induction to every new staff member.

4. Check the asbestos register before any work disturbing a fabric surface at an in-scope site.

5. Follow the Lone Worker Devices Policy's device and check-in call requirement.

6. Know the manual fallback process for a critical system outage.

Leave and absence

Annual leave entitlement is set out in each employee's own contract and requested through the standard leave request process; sickness absence is reported to the registered manager as early as possible on the first day of absence, now with a wellbeing check-in offered as part of the return-to-work process.

Standards of conduct

Every employee is expected to treat a resident, colleague, and visitor with dignity and respect at all times, to act within the boundaries of their own training and competence, and to raise a concern honestly rather than conceal it.

Health and safety responsibilities

Every employee has a personal responsibility to work safely, to report a hazard or near-miss promptly, and to follow the specific safety procedure relevant to their role; the Health and Safety Policy (Full Manual) sets out the complete framework.

Safeguarding responsibilities

Every employee has a personal responsibility to report a safeguarding concern immediately to their registered manager, following the Adult Safeguarding Policy.

Equality, diversity and inclusion

Alderbridge is committed to treating every employee and resident fairly regardless of a protected characteristic; a concern about discrimination or unfair treatment is raised with Human Resources and taken seriously.

Confidentiality and data protection

An employee has access to confidential information about a resident, a colleague, or Alderbridge's own business in the course of their role; this information is shared only on a need-to-know basis and never disclosed outside of work.

Use of Alderbridge equipment and systems

Alderbridge equipment is provided for legitimate work purposes; reasonable personal use of a shared computer is generally acceptable where it does not interfere with work or breach confidentiality.

Grievance and dispute resolution

Where an employee has a concern about their treatment at work, they are encouraged to raise it informally with their registered manager in the first instance; where this does not resolve the matter, the formal Grievance Procedure sets out the full process.

Training and development

Every employee completes mandatory training relevant to their role as part of induction and on an ongoing refresher basis; a development conversation takes place at least annually as part of the appraisal process.

Uniform and appearance

Where a role requires a uniform, this is provided by Alderbridge and is expected to be worn clean and in good repair; general appearance standards are set out in the Dress and Appearance Guidance.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. The individual moving and handling risk assessment in detail

Every MHRA records, at minimum, the person's current weight-bearing ability, their level of cooperation and understanding of what is being asked of them, the specific equipment required (including sling size and hoist type where relevant), the number of staff required, any specific technique variation (for example, a preferred side to approach from following a stroke), and the date of the last review; a care worker unfamiliar with a person for the first time (for example, covering an unfamiliar shift) is expected to read the full MHRA before providing any assistance, not only a summary or a colleague's verbal description of what is normally done.

When an MHRA needs an urgent, unscheduled review

An MHRA is reviewed immediately, not at the next routine 6-month point, following any fall, any hospital admission, any surgery, or any other event that could plausibly have changed a person's mobility, strength, or cooperation; the registered manager is responsible for identifying when such a trigger has occurred and ensuring the review happens before the person is next assisted to move, even where this means a temporary, more cautious default technique is used in the interim while the full review is arranged.

Bariatric and specialist equipment needs

Where a person's weight or body shape means standard equipment is not suitable, a specialist bariatric assessment is arranged, specifying bariatric-rated hoists, slings and, where needed, wider doorways or reinforced flooring; this assessment is treated with particular care and dignity, discussed sensitively with the person and their family, and reviewed by the Health and Safety Lead directly rather than left solely to the site's own moving and handling champion given the additional equipment and structural considerations involved.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out the waking check standard for night staff at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site running an overnight shift.

Policy statement

Every resident is checked by night staff at intervals of no more than 2 hours, or more often if their individual care plan says so, balancing a resident's need for undisturbed sleep with the safety benefit of a regular check.

Definitions

**Waking check** a check where the staff member confirms the resident's wellbeing sufficiently to be satisfied they are safe, without necessarily fully waking a sleeping resident unnecessarily. **Individual care plan interval** a shorter interval than the standard 2 hours, specified for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking.

Roles and responsibilities

**Night staff** check every resident at intervals of no more than 2 hours, recording each check. **The registered nurse or senior carer** sets an individual care plan interval for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking. **The registered manager** reviews waking check records as part of routine night-shift oversight.

1. Check every resident at intervals of no more than 2 hours through the night.
2. Follow a shorter, individually specified interval where a resident's care plan says so.
3. Record each check at the time it is completed, not retrospectively at the end of the shift.
4. Escalate immediately to the registered nurse or on-call manager if a check reveals a concern.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident is receiving end of life care and their care plan specifies a different, individually agreed checking approach, this takes precedence over the standard 2-hour interval, reflecting the different priorities appropriate to that stage of care.

Purpose and scope

This guidance sets out first aid provision at every Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift, ensuring appropriate first aid cover is always available.

Policy statement

Every shift has access to a trained first aider and a stocked first aid box, so that an injury to a resident, staff member or visitor can be responded to promptly and competently.

Definitions

**First aider** a staff member holding a current first aid at work qualification. **Appointed person** a staff member responsible for calling emergency services and looking after first aid equipment, where a full first aider is not required by the site's risk assessment. **First aid box** the stocked, clearly labelled box maintained at each site.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

HR reviews every disciplinary outcome quarterly across all sites, specifically checking for consistency in how similar conduct has been treated at different sites, and reports a summarised, anonymised picture to the Chief Executive twice a year.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

Policy statement

A body map provides a clear, dated, consistent record of a mark's location, size and appearance, supporting both good skin care and, where relevant, a safeguarding referral, since a vague written description alone can be hard to compare accurately over time.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. An MHRA is reviewed immediately, not at the next routine 6-month point, following any fall, any hospital admission, any surgery, or any other event that could plausibly have changed a person's mobility, strength, or cooperation; the registered manager is responsible for identifying when such a trigger has occurred and ensuring the review happens before the person is next assisted to move, even where this means a temporary, more cautious default technique is used in the interim while the full review is arranged.

Where a person's weight or body shape means standard equipment is not suitable, a specialist bariatric assessment is arranged, specifying bariatric-rated hoists, slings and, where needed, wider doorways or reinforced flooring; this assessment is treated with particular care and dignity, discussed sensitively with the person and their family, and reviewed by the Health and Safety Lead directly rather than left solely to the site's own moving and handling champion given the additional equipment and structural considerations involved.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out the waking check standard for night staff at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site running an overnight shift.

Policy statement

Every resident is checked by night staff at intervals of no more than 2 hours, or more often if their individual care plan says so, balancing a resident's need for undisturbed sleep with the safety benefit of a regular check.

Definitions

**Waking check** a check where the staff member confirms the resident's wellbeing sufficiently to be satisfied they are safe, without necessarily fully waking a sleeping resident unnecessarily. **Individual care plan interval** a shorter interval than the standard 2 hours, specified for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking.

Roles and responsibilities

**Night staff** check every resident at intervals of no more than 2 hours, recording each check. **The registered nurse or senior carer** sets an individual care plan interval for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking. **The registered manager** reviews waking check records as part of routine night-shift oversight.

1. Check every resident at intervals of no more than 2 hours through the night.
2. Follow a shorter, individually specified interval where a resident's care plan says so.
3. Record each check at the time it is completed, not retrospectively at the end of the shift.
4. Escalate immediately to the registered nurse or on-call manager if a check reveals a concern.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident is receiving end of life care and their care plan specifies a different, individually agreed checking approach, this takes precedence over the standard 2-hour interval, reflecting the different priorities appropriate to that stage of care.

All staff complete equality, dignity and respect training at induction and refresher training every 2 years, and managers complete additional training on handling a discrimination or harassment complaint fairly.

A worked example illustrates that this policy's dignity commitment applies to people supported, not only staff. A resident at Riverside House living with a visual impairment finds it increasingly difficult to identify her own room among several similar doors on her corridor. Rather than treating this as an inevitable consequence of her condition, staff introduce a simple, high-contrast tactile marker on her door, chosen together with her rather than imposed, and the change is recorded in her care plan as a reasonable adjustment. The registered manager subsequently reviews whether other residents on the same corridor might benefit from a similar approach, rather than treating the adjustment as a one-off fix specific to a single request.

Stock discrepancy investigation

Any stock discrepancy identified at a weekly count is investigated the same day by the registered manager, checking administration records first before considering whether an ordering or delivery error explains the gap, since most discrepancies trace back to a simple recording error rather than a genuine loss.

Governance and reporting

HR reviews every disciplinary outcome quarterly across all sites, specifically checking for consistency in how similar conduct has been treated at different sites, and reports a summarised, anonymised picture to the Chief Executive twice a year.

Appendix: the staged process at a glance

This appendix summarises the staged process described above for quick reference. An informal conversation, recorded briefly, is the starting point for most minor concerns. A first written warning follows a formal hearing where informal action has not resolved a genuine concern, and stays live for 6 months. A final written warning follows a further offence during that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, and stays live for 12 months. Dismissal with notice may follow a further offence while a final warning is live. Dismissal without notice may follow a single act of gross misconduct, at any stage, without needing to pass through the earlier stages first. An appeal is available at every formal stage, heard by a manager not previously involved, and its outcome is final within Alderbridge's own internal process, though an employee retains whatever external legal rights apply regardless of the outcome of an internal appeal.

An investigation gathers evidence objectively, seeking information that might support the employee's account as diligently as information that might support the allegation, and is completed by someone with no personal involvement in the matter and, wherever practicable, no direct reporting line to the employee concerned, so that both the fact and the appearance of a fair, independent process are preserved.

The individual moving and handling risk assessment in detail

Every MHRA records, at minimum, the person's current weight-bearing ability, their level of cooperation and understanding of what is being asked of them, the specific equipment required (including sling size and hoist type where relevant), the number of staff required, any specific technique variation (for example, a preferred side to approach from following a stroke), and the date of the last review; a care worker unfamiliar with a person for the first time (for example, covering an unfamiliar shift) is expected to read the full MHRA before providing any assistance, not only a summary or a colleague's verbal description of what is normally done.

When an MHRA needs an urgent, unscheduled review

An MHRA is reviewed immediately, not at the next routine 6-month point, following any fall, any hospital admission, any surgery, or any other event that could plausibly have changed a person's mobility, strength, or cooperation; the registered manager is responsible for identifying when such a trigger has occurred and ensuring the review happens before the person is next assisted to move, even where this means a temporary, more cautious default technique is used in the interim while the full review is arranged.

Bariatric and specialist equipment needs

Where a person's weight or body shape means standard equipment is not suitable, a specialist bariatric assessment is arranged, specifying bariatric-rated hoists, slings and, where needed, wider doorways or reinforced flooring; this assessment is treated with particular care and dignity, discussed sensitively with the person and their family, and reviewed by the Health and Safety Lead directly rather than left solely to the site's own moving and handling champion given the additional equipment and structural considerations involved.

First Aid Provision: Who to Contact

Purpose and scope

This guidance sets out first aid provision at every Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift, ensuring appropriate first aid cover is always available.

Policy statement

Every shift has access to a trained first aider and a stocked first aid box, so that an injury to a resident, staff member or visitor can be responded to promptly and competently.

Definitions

**First aider** a staff member holding a current first aid at work qualification. **Appointed person** a staff member responsible for calling emergency services and looking after first aid equipment, where a full first aider is not required by the site's risk assessment. **First aid box** the stocked, clearly labelled box maintained at each site.

1. Ensure at least one qualified first aider is on duty for every shift, based on the site's own risk assessment of resident numbers and needs.
2. Check the first aid box monthly, restocking any used or expired item promptly.
3. Record every first aid incident, however minor, in the accident book kept alongside the first aid box.
4. Call emergency services immediately for any injury beyond what first aid can safely manage.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (governing the wider incident record a first aid event also feeds into) and the Health and Safety Policy (the broader risk assessment first aid provision sits within).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates prompt response. A staff member cuts their hand while assisting in the kitchen. The on-duty first aider treats the cut using the first aid box, records it in the accident book, and confirms the box needs a replacement dressing at the next monthly check.

Worked example

Frequently asked questions

**Does every single staff member need a first aid qualification?** No, only enough trained first aiders to meet the site's risk assessment for every shift; other staff know who the first aider on duty is. **What happens if the qualified first aider is off sick unexpectedly?** The registered manager arranges cover from another qualified first aider, including from a neighbouring site if needed for that shift.

Training and competency

First aiders renew their qualification before it expires, tracked centrally by HR alongside the wider Mandatory Training Matrix.

Locating first aid equipment across a larger site

A larger site such as Harbour View holds a first aid box at more than one location given its size, and staff are shown the location nearest their usual working area during induction so a first aider is never searching for equipment while also managing an active injury.

Closing note

Prompt, competent first aid response depends on the right person and the right equipment being available every shift, and this guidance exists to make sure that is never left to chance.

Auditing COSHH practice, not only paperwork

The annual COSHH audit includes direct observation of staff actually using a hazardous substance, not
only a paper check that the register and SDS documents are present and current, since a fully compliant
paper record can still coexist with a practical habit (for example, PPE being put on inconsistently) that only
direct observation would reveal, and any such gap found is corrected through immediate coaching rather
than waiting for the next scheduled training refresher.

Substances used in activities and hobbies

Craft and activity sessions occasionally use substances (for example, certain paints or adhesives) that
also fall under COSHH; the activities coordinator checks any new material against the COSHH process
before introducing it to a session, applying the same standard to a seemingly low-risk hobby material as to
an industrial cleaning product, since the underlying legal and safety principle does not distinguish between
the two based on how harmless a substance might intuitively seem.

First Aid Provision: Who to Contact

Purpose and scope

This guidance sets out first aid provision at every Alderbridge site. It applies to every shift, ensuring appropriate first aid cover is always available.

Policy statement

Every shift has access to a trained first aider and a stocked first aid box, so that an injury to a resident, staff member or visitor can be responded to promptly and competently.

Definitions

**First aider** a staff member holding a current first aid at work qualification. **Appointed person** a staff member responsible for calling emergency services and looking after first aid equipment, where a full first aider is not required by the site's risk assessment. **First aid box** the stocked, clearly labelled box maintained at each site.

1. Ensure at least one qualified first aider is on duty for every shift, based on the site's own risk assessment of resident numbers and needs.
2. Check the first aid box monthly, restocking any used or expired item promptly.
3. Record every first aid incident, however minor, in the accident book kept alongside the first aid box.
4. Call emergency services immediately for any injury beyond what first aid can safely manage.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (governing the wider incident record a first aid event also feeds into) and the Health and Safety Policy (the broader risk assessment first aid provision sits within).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates prompt response. A staff member cuts their hand while assisting in the kitchen. The on-duty first aider treats the cut using the first aid box, records it in the accident book, and confirms the box needs a replacement dressing at the next monthly check.

Auditing COSHH practice, not only paperwork

The annual COSHH audit includes direct observation of staff actually using a hazardous substance, not
only a paper check that the register and SDS documents are present and current, since a fully compliant
paper record can still coexist with a practical habit (for example, PPE being put on inconsistently) that only
direct observation would reveal, and any such gap found is corrected through immediate coaching rather
than waiting for the next scheduled training refresher.

Substances used in activities and hobbies

Craft and activity sessions occasionally use substances (for example, certain paints or adhesives) that
also fall under COSHH; the activities coordinator checks any new material against the COSHH process
before introducing it to a session, applying the same standard to a seemingly low-risk hobby material as to
an industrial cleaning product, since the underlying legal and safety principle does not distinguish between
